intent: On a Penney Farms lot, does digging a turf base near big trees need a town permit, how much of the site can be hard surface, and does that change for a typical in-town house lot versus a larger or institutional/commercial parcel?
distinctValue: Penney Farms is an incorporated town with its own Land Development Regulations (adopted 6/28/2006, updated 4/20/2020), so the county rules its neighbours' pages turn on do not govern here: Asbury Lake's page rests on Clay County's Greater Lake Asbury District tree preservation plan (which leaves Penney Farms out), Middleburg's on the county irrigation ordinance, Ortega sand and the Black Creek gauge, Hibernia's on the St. Johns flood elevation and Blanton sand. The town's LDR 5.01.01 counts root damage from heavy machinery and changing the natural grade above the roots as removing a tree, requires a permit to remove a listed protected tree (oaks, bays, magnolia 12 in. DBH or larger; maple, sweet gum, hickory, elm, sycamore 18 in. or larger, DBH at 54 in.), and exempts lots in residential districts under one acre. The code's own minimum lot sizes put a typical in-town house under that acre: Low Density Residential lots run 21,000 sq ft minimum (6.01.01 D.2) and Medium-Low 7,000 sq ft (6.01.01 E.2), while only Rural Density Residential is sized at a full acre (43,560 sq ft, 6.01.01 C.2). The town's 2046 Comprehensive Plan's residential density policy (L.1.1.1) names Low density and Medium low density as the residential categories on the current Future Land Use Map, alongside Institutional, Commercial Town, Commercial Highway, Recreation, Utilities and Mixed Use; it does not list a Rural category, so which lots (if any) are still mapped Rural is a Town Hall question, not one this page can settle from the plan text alone. LDR 6.01.02 caps the impervious surface ratio by district (0.35 rural, 0.40 low, 0.50 medium-low, 0.70 commercial, industrial and institutional) and excludes porous paving built to town standards. Development includes excavating, grading and installing impervious surface; permits go through the Town Clerk and Building Inspector; the Site Clearing/Site Work Application asks for FLUM designation and acreage and has a 14 business day completeness review. Water is the town's own: two Floridan Aquifer wells; the operative development restriction (5.04.02 A) sets a 50 ft no-development zone around a public well, while the code's own Article II definition separately calls the same area a 200 ft 'zone of exclusion' — the page states both numbers rather than picking one. A 300 ft zone bars excavated drainage that intersects the water table. USDA soils inside the town limits are Hurricane fine sand (water table to 69 cm) at the Census internal point and Leon fine sand (31 cm) just south. Underneath the town's own rules, Florida Rule 62-308.100 (effective 19 May 2026) and s. 125.572, F.S. stop a local government from prohibiting turf that meets the state infill standard on a single-family lot of an acre or less; Penney Farms doesn't prohibit turf outright, so this floor doesn't reach the tree or coverage rules above it, and the page says so rather than implying the state rule overrides the town code.

sources.label: Town of Penney Farms Land Development Regulations (adopted 6/28/2006, updated 4/20/2020)
supports: Cover: "TOWN OF PENNEY FARMS Land Development Regulations Adopted - 6/28/2006 Updated - 4/20/2020"

5.01.01 Removal Of Trees, A: "Removal of a tree includes any act which will cause a tree to die, such as damage inflicted upon the root system by heavy machinery, changing the natural grade above the root system or round the trunk, damage, including fire damage, inflicted on the tree permitting infection or pest infestation."

5.01.01 B: "It shall be unlawful for any person, organization, society, association or corporation or any agent or representative thereof, directly or indirectly, to cut down, destroy, remove or move, or effectively destroy through damaging any protected tree listed below located on any property without obtaining a permit except for lots in residential districts under one (1) acre."

5.01.01 B table: "Turkey Oak (Quercus laevis) 12" or larger; Other Oak Species (Quercus spp.) 12" or larger; Maple (Acer spp.) 18" or larger; Sweet Gum 18" or larger; Hickory 18" or larger; Elm (Ulmus spp.) 18" or larger; Lobloly Bay 12" or larger; Sweet Bay 12" or larger; Real Bay (Persea borbonia) 12" or larger; Swamp Bay (Persea palustris) 12" or larger; Sycamore (Platanus occidentalis) 18" or larger; Magnolia 12" or larger"

5.01.03 A: "In respect to removal of a protected tree to allow construction of improvements, as a condition for granting a permit, the Town Council shall require the developer to replace the protected tree with the installation of new trees. The number and location of new trees shall be based on a site plan submitted by the developer and approved by the council."

Article II definition: "DBH - Diameter at breast height. "Breast height" is defined to be fifty-four (54) inches above the surface of the ground at the base of the plant or tree. In the case of a tree with multiple main stems, the diameter shall be the sum of the diameters of the stems."

Article II definition: "Protected Tree - Any tree that has a DBH of more than eight (8) inches, and which is not otherwise exempted from this Code. In addition, all palms with at least four and one-half (4 1/2) feet of clear trunk between the ground level and the lowest branch are declared to be protected trees."

Article II definition: "Tree Protection Zone - A circular zone around each protected tree. If the drip line is less than six (6) feet from the trunk of the tree, the zone shall be that area within a radius of six (6) feet around the tree. If the drip line is more than six (6) feet from the trunk of the tree, but less than twenty (20) feet, the zone shall be that area within a radius of the full drip line around the tree. If the drip line is twenty (20) feet or more from the trunk of the tree, the zone shall be that area within a radius of twenty (20) feet around the tree."

Article II definition: "Development or Development Activity - Any of the following activities: 1. Construction, clearing, filling, excavating, grading, paving, dredging, mining, drilling or otherwise significantly disturbing the soil of a site. 2. Building, installing, enlarging, replacing or substantially restoring a structure, impervious surface, or water management system ... 4. A tree removal for which authorization is required under this Code."

Article II definition: "Impervious Surface - A surface that has been compacted or covered with a layer of material so that it is highly resistant to infiltration by water. It includes, but is not limited to, semi-impervious surfaces such as compacted clay, as well as most conventionally surfaced streets, roofs, sidewalks, parking lots and other similar structures."
Article II definition: "Wellhead Protection Area, Zone Of Exclusion - All land within a two hundred (200) foot radius of an existing or designated protected wellhead."
6.01.01 C: "Specific Requirements for Rural Density Residential 1.Mobile Homes - 1 acre of land 2. Minimum Lot Area - 43,560 square feet"

6.01.01 D.2: "Every lot or parcel of land shall have an area of not less than twenty one thousand (21,000) square feet and a frontage at the building line of at least one hundred (100) feet." (Low Density Residential)

6.01.01 E.2: "Every lot or parcel of land shall have an area of not less than seven thousand (7,000) square feet and a frontage at the building line of at least seventy (70) feet." (Medium-Low Density)

6.01.02 B: "The impervious surface ratio is calculated by dividing the total impervious surface by the gross site area." C: "If porous paving materials are used in accord with the standards approved by the Town, then the area covered with porous paving materials shall not be counted as impervious surface."
6.01.02 D Table of Impervious Surface Ratios: "Rural Density Residential 0.35; Low Density Residential 0.40; Medium-Low Residential 0.50; Commercial 0.70; Industrial 0.70; Institutional 0.70"

5.04.02 A: "No development activities shall take place in the zone of exclusion which is the area within 50 feet of a public drinking well." B: "The following land uses are prohibited within Wellhead Protection Zone, the area within 300 feet of a public drinking well: ... 7. Excavation of waterways or drainage facilities which intersect the water table."

6.06.01 Exemption: "Lots or parcels of land on which a single family home is used as a residence shall be exempt from all provisions of these landscaping regulations. This shall not be construed to exempt any residential developments that require the approval of a development plan."

6.06.04 C: "All landscaped areas shall be provided with an appropriate irrigation system that conforms to the standards approved by the Town of Penney Farms. If a landscaped area contains primarily species native to the immediate region, or plants acceptable for xeric landscaping, the Town, may waive the requirement for installation of an irrigation system." D Non-Living Materials: "Mulches shall be a minimum depth of two (2) inches and plastic surface covers shall not be used."
12.01.01: "No development activity may be undertaken unless the activity is authorized by a development permit."

12.05.01: "Application for a Development Permit shall be made to the Town Clerk on a form provided by the town and may be acted upon by the town without public hearing or notice." 12.05.02: "The Building Inspector appointed by the town shall review all applications for development permits prior to issuance of the permits by the Town Clerk."

sources.label: Rule 62-308.100, F.A.C. — adopted rule text, Florida Administrative Code
supports: Rule record: Chapter 62-308, "Minimum Standards for the Installation of Synthetic Turf on Specified Properties". Effective Date: 5/19/2026. History note "History–New 5-19-26". Rulemaking Authority and Law Implemented: 125.572 FS.

Adopted text, paragraph (2)(c): "Infill material, if used, shall only be clean silica sand, rock, shell, or other natural material, except that coated silica sand may be used provided that any coating used is non-toxic..."

s. 125.572(3)(a), Florida Statutes, is the law the rule implements: it bars a local government from prohibiting synthetic turf on single-family residential property, on a lot of one acre or less, when that turf complies with the DEP standards adopted under the section — reused here from the same primary source already vetted and cited for the site's Florida Turf Infill Rules guide (src/data/guides.ts).

Point -81.8106, 29.9769 (Census geocoder returns "Penney Farms town", Clay County): mukey 132854 "Leon fine sand, 0 to 2 percent slopes", component Leon 89%, "Poorly drained", hydrologic group A/D, "Sandy, siliceous, thermic Aeric Alaquods", minimum wet-season soil moisture depth 31 cm, flooding frequency "None".
